THE BRIEF

Take something familiar. Question everything about it.

Redefine is a 24-hour designathon where creativity meets innovation, challenging participants to rethink the digital experiences they interact with every day.

Rather than simply improving existing platforms, participants are encouraged to question established design patterns, challenge assumptions, and reimagine how technology can serve users in entirely new ways.

From reinventing Spotify and transforming e-commerce to redesigning social platforms, productivity tools, entertainment experiences, or everyday applications, the possibilities are limitless. The goal is not to build another version of what already exists, but to create something bold, meaningful, and distinctly different.

Throughout the 24-hour challenge, participants will explore user experience, visual design, interaction design, and emerging technologies to turn unconventional ideas into compelling digital experiences. They will identify limitations in familiar platforms, rethink their core interactions, and develop solutions that are intuitive, engaging, accessible, and future-ready.

Redefine is ultimately about breaking away from the expected. It provides a space for designers, developers, innovators, and creative thinkers to experiment beyond conventional boundaries and transform ambitious ideas into tangible experiences.

At Redefine, there are no fixed answers. The challenge is simple: take something familiar, question everything about it, and build something better.

JUDGING

Four things the judges score

Craft carries as much weight as the idea. A radical concept in careless type and colour won’t clear the bar — and neither will a beautiful screen that changes nothing.

Criterion 01

Architecture

How the experience is structured — information hierarchy, navigation, and whether the flow holds up under real use.

Criterion 02

Colour Palette

Deliberate colour with a working system behind it: contrast, accessibility, and a palette chosen for this product.

Criterion 03

Typography

Type as a decision, not a default. Scale, pairing, weight, spacing, and readability across the whole interface.

Criterion 04

Creativity

How far you moved from the original. The bolder the departure — and the better you justify it — the higher this scores.

TEAM UP

Teams are one to four

Enter solo or bring up to three others. Everyone on the team registers individually, and you name your team when you do — put the same team name on every entry so we can group you.

Solo

1 member

A valid entry. You compete on the same criteria as everyone else, on the same clock.

Small

2–3 members

The common shape. Enough to split research, visual design and prototyping without losing time to coordination.

Full

4 members

The maximum. Worth it if you can genuinely parallelise — twenty-four hours punishes teams that can’t.

FAQ

Before you ask

Anything not covered here goes out to registered teams by email before the 16th.

What does it cost?

₹150 per ticket. That’s per person, and it covers the full 24 hours at the venue.

Can I enter on my own?

Yes. Teams are 1 to 4 members, so a solo entry is a valid team.

Is this a coding event?

It’s a designathon. The judging criteria are architecture, colour palette, typography and creativity — so the work is judged as design. How far you take it into a working prototype is up to you and your team.

What will I be designing?

A set of tracks is announced at the start of the event, and your team chooses one of them to work in. Expect familiar territory — music and streaming, e-commerce, social platforms, productivity tools, entertainment, everyday apps. Whichever track you pick, the rule is the same: you’re replacing something familiar, not polishing it.

Can I start designing before the event?

The brief drops at 08:00 on 16 September and the clock starts there. Coming in with sharpened tools, a set-up file and a point of view is fine; coming in with the deliverable is not.

Where exactly is it?

Sarojini Naidu Gallery, from 08:00 AM on 16 September to 08:00 AM on 17 September. Reporting time and what to bring will be sent to registered teams.
